OSINTdefender The 8th Circuit Court of Appeals has denied the emergency stay request and lifted its administrative stay of the permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, clearing the way for the U.S. Army's controlled detonation of 68 barrels containing a 9,773lbs of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, near Middletown. The court found the permit's safeguards adequate. They include containment barriers, weather restrictions, public notification, and lead sampling and cleanup requirements. Both sides agreed the detonation will cause some public harm. The court said the real choice was between a controlled detonation with mitigation in place and an uncontrolled explosion with none. The Army had said it intends to act by November 25th. tweet

South Korea said a suspected North Korean aircraft violated its airspace near an eastern island on Tuesday, prompting authorities to issue a shelter-in-place order for residents. Officials initially identified the aircraft as Russian and instructed residents of Ulleung Island to seek shelter in underground facilities or nearby buildings. The evacuation order was later lifted after the government revised its assessment, saying the aircraft may have been North Korean.
